<details id="dependency-88d694773a43e24bfc8a9702c141ffe64c59154c646c8cf9404ba538e68936be-details" class="dependency-details">
<summary id="dependency-88d694773a43e24bfc8a9702c141ffe64c59154c646c8cf9404ba538e68936be-summary" class="dependency-summary" aria-label="Details for com.google.guava:listenablefuture:jar:9999.0-empty-to-avoid-conflict-with-guava">Details</summary>
<div class="dependency-metadata">
<p>An empty artifact that Guava depends on to signal that it is providing ListenableFuture -- but is also available in a second &quot;version&quot; that contains com.google.common.util.concurrent.ListenableFuture class, without any other Guava classes. The idea is: - If users want only ListenableFuture, they depend on listenablefuture-1.0. - If users want all of Guava, they depend on guava, which, as of Guava 27.0, depends on listenablefuture-9999.0-empty-to-avoid-conflict-with-guava. The 9999.0-... version number is enough for some build systems (notably, Gradle) to select that empty artifact over the &quot;real&quot; listenablefuture-1.0 -- avoiding a conflict with the copy of ListenableFuture in guava itself. If users are using an older version of Guava or a build system other than Gradle, they may see class conflicts. If so, they can solve them by manually excluding the listenablefuture artifact or manually forcing their build systems to use 9999.0-....</p>
<dl>
<dt>Upstream project name</dt>
<dd>Guava ListenableFuture only</dd>
<dt>Resolved coordinate</dt>

<dt>Artifact type</dt>
<dd>jar</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</details>
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</section>

<div class="dependency-metadata">
<p>JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a lightweight data-interchange format. It is easy for humans to read and write. It is easy for machines to parse and generate. It is based on a subset of the JavaScript Programming Language, Standard ECMA-262 3rd Edition - December 1999. JSON is a text format that is completely language independent but uses conventions that are familiar to programmers of the C-family of languages, including C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Perl, Python, and many others. These properties make JSON an ideal data-interchange language.</p>
<dl>

## About this inventory

**Maven** supplies the mediated graph and effective POM metadata, including inherited license declarations.
This inventory describes the source revision of this documentation version; retained release snapshots
preserve their own inventory. Each entry identifies a resolved group, artifact, type, optional classifier,
and version. Effective scope and type come from that graph node, not its parent or the dependency POM's
packaging. Runtime groups `compile` and `runtime`; Test contains `test`. Provided and system dependencies
appear separately when present. Direct dependencies are declared by this project; transitive dependencies
are brought in through other project dependencies.

Entries show artifact IDs, with group IDs when an artifact ID repeats. Full upstream project names and
resolved coordinates remain in Details. Direct dependencies appear first; each subgroup is sorted by
artifact ID, with full coordinates breaking ties.

This inventory excludes build plugins, annotation processors configured outside the project dependency
graph, and the documentation/tooling **npm** and Python environments. It is not an inventory of every build tool.
License names and URLs reproduce all upstream declarations without inferring an AND/OR relationship.
A metadata override fills missing licensing information only and identifies its reviewed source and reason
in the entry's details. Missing descriptive fields are labeled explicitly; they are not invented.

The tree shows Maven's mediated representative paths, not every possible dependency path or omitted conflict.
Node labels retain their own effective scopes; indentation does not determine scope. The root label is stable
across project release-version transitions.

See the [project license](licenses.md) and the
[maintenance instructions](../contributing/documentation-authoring.md#maintain-license-and-dependency-pages).
